title: ​ | Sabbath Evening Class: Secrets in the Lord's Prayer

sense.text: Tonight is the secrets of the Lord’s prayer, because we always say the Lord’s prayer, but some of us just say it without understanding. “That he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is”: that goes into how many of the scriptures in the Bible have double meanings, and it’s always that second meaning that’s often secretive.

precepts.why: “Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” We can never think that we know everything in this truth. Never think that: that’s an arrogant spirit, and the Lord said ‘speak no more arrogancy’. Many times we’ll know a few precepts and not really understand the underlying meaning of those precepts.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

Notice where it says “those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children”. The Lord don’t reveal everything at one time. He reveals it in time, in increments, and it always comes through leadership. It’s not going to come through the crackhead who came in yesterday and had a revelation. You don’t read about that in the Bible, that so-and-so came in and the Lord gave her the wisdom of what this verse is talking about. That’s why we don’t listen to a lot of foolishness: when it comes out, it’s going to come from leadership, and it’s going to be fact checked.

sense.text:
This is the famous prayer that we all pray in Israel. “Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.” Notice he says say ‘our Father’. You get many of these dumb Black Hebrew Israelites that want to say no, you got to say this name or that name. That’s why Christ said when you pray, say our Father which art in heaven.

We don’t have a problem if a brother prays and says Yahawah, or some say Yahweh in other camps. But when you start to say you must say the name that I’m giving you or else you’re condemned, that’s not in the book.

precepts.why:
“And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty”. Where it says God Almighty, in the Hebrew it says El Shaddai. Go to Ben Yehuda’s Hebrew English dictionary and it’ll tell you that El Shaddai means the terrible demon-like power, because of the flood that occurred with Noah.

“But by my name Jehovah was I not known”. The name Jehovah translated in the Lashon Kodesh is pronounced Yahawah. I did a video on that over 30 years ago and all the BHI referenced that video, and not one of them can do a better one. Translated into English it means he is, or he exists. Like the name I am, Ahaya Ashara Ahaya, means I am that I am. If I say I’m going to the store and you ask who’s going to the store, the answer is he’s going to the store: he is, meaning me. That’s all they’re saying.

“Accustom not thy mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.” You’re not supposed to always be saying the Lord’s name. We say the Lord’s name in prayers and honor and thanksgiving, not in random conversation. This is what the BHI don’t understand: you got to say the Lord’s name 26 times in the video? No you don’t. It says don’t do that. Just constantly saying it is a form of taking his name in vain.

Then they say you can’t say God, because it’s dog spelled backwards. So I can’t say kid either? Believe it or not, that was the doctrine when we came in: you were not allowed to say the word God because spelled backwards it’s dog. That’s jailhouse talk.

“For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark: so he that sweareth and nameth God continually shall not be faultless.” You won’t be faultless if you constantly name God continually: his name is this, his name is that.

“Him that overcometh”: like we got to overcome our sins, the trials and tribulations. “Will I make a pillar in the temple of my God”: a pillar, like the pillars that hold up the roof of this building, is a leader. It keeps things upright and moving. “And he shall go no more out”: out of the temple, out of the kingdom, into captivity. We ain’t going into that no more.

“And I will write upon him the name of my God”. But in Exodus 6:3 didn’t he already give the name God Almighty, El Shaddai, and then give Moses Yahawah? If we already got it, why is the Son of God saying he will give us the name, future tense? The BHI don’t believe that; they say no, we already got it.

What’s amazing is that brothers claim they got the name, yet they hate their brothers. When we came out of Egypt, we all knew that name, millions of us, and the Most High put to death that first generation and only saved Joshua and Caleb. You should read that and be ashamed.

“Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness”: the her is the Israelites; we are her. “And speak comfortably unto her”: he’s going to give us the laws and testimonies all over again. There’s things we mess up on and we might not know it. We don’t know everything: we see in part, we prophesy in part, and when that which is perfect is come we shall know even as we are known. That’s when the Lord is going to reveal to us all things. We’re not there yet.

“And the valley of Achor for a door of hope”: that’s the garden of Eden. “As in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt”: like when we came out of Egypt into the promised land.

“Thou shalt call me Ishi”: write this down, Ishi means my husband. “And shalt call me no more Baali”: Baali is all the other names we reference the Most High by today, in English or Spanish or Creole. Oh, you on the corner of 125th Street, can’t get out of your mama’s house, in poverty, but you got the supreme being’s name and nobody else got it?

“For I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth”. He did not say I will kill you for not speaking the Lashon Kodesh. He did not say I will kill you for speaking Yiddish. He said he will take away the names of Baalim: they’re going to change our language, he’s going to take that from us. “And they shall no more be remembered by their name”: we ain’t going to remember the names we use no more.

Look at all the various names the Most High is called by: El Shaddai, Lord God the Almighty; El Elyon, the high God; Adonai, Lord, Master; Yahweh, Lord, Jehovah; Jehovah Nissi, the Lord my banner; Jehovah Rapha, the Lord that heals; the Lord my shepherd; the Lord is there; the Lord our righteousness; the Lord who sanctifies you; El Olam, the everlasting God; Elohim, God; Jehovah Jireh, the Lord will provide; Jehovah Shalom, the Lord is peace; the Lord of hosts. And there’s more. ‘No, you can’t say those names, you have to say the one I’m giving you, you’re in sin if you say all those others’: that’s the most ridiculous thing. I used to teach that when I was in my 20s, that stupid Black jailhouse talk, and you’ll hear Black Israelites say it. I don’t care if you’re Puerto Rican, I’m still talking about you too. Remember, that’s why Christ said when you pray, say our Father which art in heaven.

sense.text: The Lord is teaching Isaiah how to teach us how to read the Bible. “Precept must be upon precept”: law must be upon law. “Line upon line”: a line here in this chapter, another line in another chapter; a line in the Old Testament, another line in the New Testament. “Here a little, and there a little”: here a little in this chapter, there a little in the next; here a little in the Old Testament, there a little in the New Testament. That’s how you read the Bible. It’s a puzzle.

“For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.” The Lord says I’m going to teach you in another language, because the Israelites were going into captivity, into slavery. Brazil don’t speak English, they speak Portuguese. The Netherlands speak Dutch. Over here we speak English; Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo, Spanish; Haiti, Creole. The Lord prophesied he would speak to us in another tongue, and I don’t see what’s so difficult to understand about that.

So we got to stop thinking like stupid Black people: ‘now you have to learn this language I’m going to teach you, here’s a piece of paper with all the translations.’ It makes no sense. Where in the Bible did the apostle Paul or any of them sit down and teach Hebrew to the Greek-speaking Israelites or the Latin-speaking Israelites? There’s no verse on that. We got to stop being stupid and stop listening to these camps.

The Tetragrammaton means four letters: YHWH. It is pronounced by various people various different ways. We were taught Yahawah; in Yiddish they say Yahweh; there are groups that say Yahuwah, and a whole lot more. Get yourself caught up with these groups and you’ll be arguing over the correct pronunciation. That’s just stupid. Even in Nigeria there was a brother who had another name for the Lord. We read him this verse and asked what it means, and he said you must say the name I’m giving you. If you don’t get that, you’re just stupid.

“This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest”. Our people are weary in Brazil; they need to hear the word of God in Portuguese. Our people are weary in Haiti; they need to hear the word in Creole. Our people are weary in America; we need the word in English because that’s what we understand. Our people are weary in Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo; they need to hear the word in Spanish.

“And this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.” Because no, you got to learn Hebrew, come to my Hebrew class and learn my variation of Hebrew. Y’all fall for that stuff if you want.

precepts.why:
Paul made mention of it, speaking about tongues. “In the law it is written”: notice he said in the law. You didn’t know Isaiah was the law; now you know. “With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.”

You know why people won’t hear you? Because you didn’t say the right name, brother or sister, you got to say Yahuwah. Let’s read the English because we read and understand English. ‘No brother, you can’t say God, you can’t say Lord, you must say Yahweh.’ Or what’s going to happen to me, I’m going to get struck by a bolt of lightning? Where’s the lightning? “And yet for all that will they not hear me”.

sense.text: This is the prophecy of Isaiah 28. “There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven”: these Jews came from all over. These were Israelites in captivity, released during the time of Cyrus. They came from Persia, from Iraq and Iran, and it’s going to name all the places as we read down.
They were all there to celebrate Pentecost. “Every man heard them speak in his own language”: how do we hear these men speaking in our language?
“Are not all these which speak Galileans?” You Galileans got a different form of the Hebrew; you don’t even speak the way we do.

“And how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born?” We hear you perfect in the language we were born in. That’s why it’s important to translate into the language the people were born in. That’s called their first language: they were raised in it from a baby and they understand it. A secondary language will cause problems.

I worked at a high school many years ago in Washington Heights, and the students wanted to take the state exam in Spanish, because Spanish is their mother language. The dean said we don’t think you want it in Spanish. They insisted, so they brought the exams in Spanish, but it was the Spanish from Spain, Castilian Spanish. Totally different. Everybody failed, and the parents came to the school cursing in Spanish and English. You can’t make this stuff up. One Spanish is different from Puerto Rican Spanish, like Creole is different from French.

So the Lord wanted the gospel to be preached in their first language.

“Parthians, and Medes”: that’s around Iran. The Israelites that came from Iran with the Holy Spirit on them had to teach and preach in that dialect, not in any form of Hebrew, and when they got to Lord or God it had to be translated in that Iranian language so they knew exactly what was being talked about. “And Elamites”: that’s East India. “And the dwellers in Mesopotamia”: that’s Babylon, Iraq. If you came from East India or Iraq, you heard the gospel in your first tongue, your mother language, not in Hebrew. “And in Judea”: that’s Hebrew. “And Cappadocia”: that’s Turkey.

“In Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene”: Libya, that’s North Africa. Whatever language they were born in, the gospel was taught in that language. They didn’t stop and say let me give you the Hebrew name for God. You won’t read that in here. That’s why Christ said when you pray, say our Father which art in heaven. “And strangers of Rome”: that’s Latin.

“Cretes and Arabians”: Crete is in Greece, and Arabians, that’s their Arabic dialect. “We do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God.” This cuts down the doctrine that you must speak Hebrew today. The wonderful works of God were spoken in all languages; it’s telling you that in English right there in the Bible.

precepts.why: Christ was on the cross: “Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” The proper translation is my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me. But “some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, This man calleth for Elias.” They thought he was calling on Elijah the prophet. That misunderstanding shows you there was a difference in the Hebrew pronunciation at that time; they spoke a different kind of Hebrew. So let’s stop being Black people from the jailhouse.

sense.text: “Thy kingdom come.” We always pray thy kingdom come, but what does it mean? Daniel 2 is going to explain thy kingdom come. When you pray thy kingdom come, you’re asking for the destruction of the nations. The Christian church don’t understand that: you’re asking for the Lord to destroy all the nations.

Nebuchadnezzar had a dream about this huge statue and he couldn’t remember it. Daniel had to come in and tell him what the dream was, and then translate the dream for him. “His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.”

“A stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.” At the end there’s going to be a stone cut out without hands that’s going to smite the feet of this image and break it in pieces. “And the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.”

Now we get the interpretation. “Thou art this head of gold.” Daniel the prophet reveals that Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon represents the head of gold. Babylon ruled from about 606 to about 529 BC.

“And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee”: the next kingdom that came after Babylon was the Medo-Persian captivity, with Cyrus. When y’all saw the movie 300, that was the Medo-Persian captivity going in towards the Greek. “And another third kingdom of brass”: the third kingdom of brass began with Alexander the Great. The Greeks represented the brass, and in 300 you see the Spartans, which is supposed to be us, fighting against the Persians.
“And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron”: the iron represents Rome. You had two forms of Rome, the Roman republic and then the Roman empire. That movie Gladiator was the Roman republic.

“The feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided”: the feet of iron and clay are the divided kingdoms of the revived Roman empire, America and Europe. “There shall be in it of the strength of the iron”: that iron is military. America and Europe have the most powerful military in the world, starting with America.

The ten toes, write this down, represent the ten common markets, also called the EU, the European Union. Not the African Union, not the Chinese union, not the Arab union. Revelation calls them ten horns; Daniel calls them the ten toes. The originals were Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland. There’s more than ten now, but those were the beginning. “So the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.”

“They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men”: all different nations. Europe is more integrated than America. Look at the movies from Europe or the UK and you’ll see Arabs and Asians growing up with Black people, married to Black people, having kids with Black people; it’s total confusion over there. At least America is a little more segregated, except when the ball players make money.

Another example: they brought thousands of Afghans to America, giving them grants to learn English, money for business, for living arrangements and food. Then the Haitians came. Haitian migrants trying to escape poverty and hunger crossed from Mexico at the Texas border, and the U.S. planned to speedily send them back. Your president that your mamas voted for says get them out, the damn Haitians, get them out. If you don’t know what racism and hatred is, I can’t help you. Over 10,000 Levites are living under the bridges in parts of Texas right now, along with Zebulun and Issachar.

“But they shall not cleave one to another”: that’s why there’s no true unity between the races, no true affinity. I’m not talking about you Negroes that marry the white girl; I’m talking about between our races. There’s no true friendship, no true love. That’s why we’re always marching, no justice no peace, we shall overcome. “Even as iron is not mixed with clay”: the same way iron can’t mix with clay, the races cannot mix together. Can we all get along? God says hell no. This was inspired from Genesis: from the beginning, from the tower of Babel, God never wanted the nations to mix. It was never going to happen.

“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom”. In the days of what kings? The kings we just read about, the ten common markets, America and Europe, because that’s the time we’re living in now. The rest of them are still around too: Rome, Greece, Persia and Media, Babylon. In the days of the ten common markets he will set up a kingdom. Y’all don’t realize what you’re looking at right here: it’s just an iota, a glimmer, a speck, but this is the prophecy, the brothers and sisters online that have never even graced the doors of IUIC. He’s setting up a kingdom. You thought that’s talking about Christ’s coming; not yet. It’s going to get to Christ.

“Which shall never be destroyed”: you could take me out, you could take the bishops and the deacons, but as long as there’s one man that has a proper understanding of this Bible, it will never be destroyed.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. Some of y’all got mixed families: my mom is white. The Lord don’t give a damn about that. Your mom is not going to inherit the kingdom of heaven as a ruler. I have a good friend named Becky; the Lord don’t care about Becky either, or Karen.

“But it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.” This part goes into Christ. When you’re praying thy kingdom come, you’re asking for the destruction of the nations.

“The stone was cut out of the mountain without hands”: that’s Christ, the stone cut without hands, out of mount Zion. “And that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold”: the iron is Rome, the brass was Greece, the clay is America, the silver was Persia and Media, and the gold was Babylon. “The great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.”

precepts.why:
When Daniel prophesies this, the Christian is mad: y’all can’t be saying the races ain’t going to get together. But what Daniel prophesied is what God orchestrated from the beginning. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance”: he divided to the nations their lands. “When he separated the sons of Adam”: we all come from Babel, and he said I separated all the sons of Adam.

The Christian goes to church: that ain’t right, in Jesus’ name I declare it ain’t right. The Lord don’t give a damn what you declare in Jesus’ name. The preacher used the black highlighter over that scripture; that’s why he can’t quote it. I saw a man on the train with his Bible open, literally taking a black marker and crossing things out in his Bible.

“He set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel”: he gave us the choicest land. That’s why we had to move the Philistines and everybody out, the Canaanites: get out, it’s our land.

“It shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms”: Daniel is saying the same thing the apostle Paul said. “And then shall that Wicked be revealed”: the white man is the wicked that the Bible is talking about, and he must be revealed. “Whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth”: Christ is not on earth consuming all the nations with the spirit of his mouth. It’s us, bringing out the prophetic scriptures. We’re the ones he’s using; that’s why it starts with us. Y’all want the Lord to come down and do it. Oh no, we got to work for this thing.

“And shall destroy with the brightness of his coming”: that’s when Christ comes. He’s going to destroy them with the brightness of his coming, but he’s starting with us. You men got to get off your lazy Black ashy behinds and teach this gospel. You waiting for angels to come down and do it for you? The angels ain’t coming down doing nothing for you. Before he brings the destruction, the prerequisite is us teaching the scripture, revealing and bringing out this truth. The cart is not going to come before the horse.
The stone cut out without hands: “Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.” That’s talking about Christ.

“Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.” The one in Peter is talking about Christ, the one in Isaiah is talking about Christ, so guess who Daniel’s talking about: Christ, the stone cut out of the mountain without hands.

sense.text:
We read this one a lot; churches don’t, but we do. “I beheld till the thrones were cast down”: he’s saying the same thing he said in chapter two. I beheld till the kingdoms of the earth were cast down, meaning destroyed. That’s thy kingdom come.

“And the Ancient of days did sit”: God, having no beginning of days or end of days, sat on his throne. In order to sit, you got to have a body. “Whose garment was white as snow”: in order to have a garment on, you got to have a body. “And the hair of his head like the pure wool”: it’s telling you that God’s a Black man, straight up, no ifs and buts. He got pure wool hair. Get mad if you want.

“His throne was like the fiery flame”: fire got color to it. He got fire all around his throne; you can’t just approach him with ‘I got something to say’, you’re dead. “And his wheels as burning fire”: his wheels are the chariots. Some dumb BHI say there’s no UFOs; yes there are.

precepts.why:
I saw a video of a dumb Black Christian saying God don’t got no color. You see all this color on earth, but in heaven there’s no color? You only hear Black people say that, because white people were painting a Caucasian Jesus, a white God.

“A throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone”. Tell me what God looks like. Look at the jasper and sardine stone: see how brown they are, and some of them are darker than that. How are you going to look at that and say God is white?

“And there was a rainbow round about the throne”. A rainbow in heaven, but there ain’t no color in heaven? You’re wrong, Pookie and Ray Ray, you’re stupid too. There’s color in heaven. “In sight like unto an emerald”: emeralds are green. I thought there was no color in heaven? Simple as hell.

When the white folks and the Negroes notice this, if they concede to it they have to put down the white supremacy, which is Christianity. Christianity is the willful acceptance of white supremacy; it’s the excuse for not testing the truth of the Bible. That’s why you got to leave the Christian church. Get the hell out of the damned Christian church, and that’s right, I said damned Christian church.

The Christian church is damned, and I’m going to read the Bible for you in case you think I’m using cuss words. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion”: you know what a strong delusion is? Ain’t no color in heaven, and Jesus and the angels white: that’s a strong delusion. We got to celebrate Christmas and Thanksgiving: that’s strong delusion. “That they should believe a lie”: that Christian rhetoric is a lie.

“That they all might be damned”. God says that they all might be damned, so I’m not using a cuss word; it’s in the Bible, the New Testament, for you hypocrites. That includes some of your mothers, your fathers, your aunties, your grandmamas and grandfathers, because you showed them the truth and they said hell no, I’m going with white Jesus. Now they’re damned. Cry if you want. It’s the sisters that write the emails: can y’all pray for my grandma or my mom, she don’t want to believe the truth of the Bible. Then she’s damned. You can’t pray somebody out of a rebellious spirit; you don’t read about that in the Bible. You could pray the gay away? You keep praying; if you ain’t studying and applying it, it ain’t going nowhere.

“Until the Ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the most High”: we’re the saints. Judgment’s going to be given to us in time to come. “And the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom”: that’s the judgment we want, that we possess the kingdom.

“And the kingdom and dominion”: this is the same kingdom and dominion we read about in Daniel 2 that will never be destroyed, the same thing we read in Matthew 6, thy kingdom come. “And the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven”: under the whole heaven means the whole planet earth. “Shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High”: it’s not going to be given to the Europeans or the Chinese or the Japanese. China is not the next world superpower; that’s not in the Bible. The Bible says the saints of the Most High are the next ruling power. That’s us.

“Whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him”: everybody’s going to serve and obey the Lord, because we’re going to be God’s enforcers.

“Hitherto is the end of the matter.” You always want to stress that when you teach. That’s God’s biblical plan for this earth. There is no plan B or C. His plan is to destroy the nations and set the Israelites in authority over the whole planet.

sense.text:
We’re still dealing with Matthew 6:10, thy kingdom come. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: when we get rulership, the sons of the other nations shall build up our walls. “And their kings shall minister unto thee”: their kings shall be our servants.

“For in my wrath I smote thee”: what do you think Covid is about? What do you think slavery and oppression is about? It’s us being smitten; God has smote us. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: in his favour he had mercy on us, because he gave Christ as a sacrifice, and now he’s going to bring us out of these dark trials we’re going through, soon to come.

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually”: the gates of our kingdom are going to be open continually. “They shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the forces of the Gentiles means the wealth of the Gentiles, the riches. “And that their kings may be brought”: their kings brought in too.
“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”: any kingdom that don’t serve us, the Bible says they shall perish. “Yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. We’re not really a thinking people. Do you think Lebanon is going to willingly bring the fir trees and the pine trees to beautify God’s sanctuary? No. The Lord is going to dispatch a small regiment of men to Lebanon and make them bring the trees. It might just be 20 brothers; that’s all the Lord needs, you don’t need 500. Remember how two could chase a thousand.

We’re going to be sent: these are the trees we want, and you’re going to bring them on this day. No, we will not? Okay, off with their heads, everybody dead; that’s your wife, off with her head too; all those little kids, all dead. Anybody else got something to say? Oh no, we will bring the trees tomorrow. That’s what they’re going to do: everybody is going to be willing. “And I will make the place of my feet glorious.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee”: yes, you can include Ishmael. Dumb damn Arabs: in the Deaconess’s class the brother was blasting one who called us racist, while the same white man standing next to him, the Israeli, is blowing up his so-called country and throwing him out of Palestine, and he didn’t know what to say.

They’re going to come bending, not straight up looking us in the eye. You better bow, bend the knees, and not one knee: “and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet”. Both knees, with their face to the ground. “And they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

“Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated”: right now it looks like we’re a forsaken people. We are a hated people; don’t nobody love us, and it even looks like the Lord don’t love us. But in our understanding he’s saying, I’m giving you my word right now: build your spirits up, build your families up, prepare yourself for my second return. “I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.”

“Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles”: that’s their wealth. “And shalt suck the breast of kings: and thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.”

“For brass I will bring gold”: a lot of us got little brass, like this little armband. The Lord says for brass I’m going to bring gold; it might not be this day, but in the kingdom all these little brass studs are going to be gold. All these black women got these damn brass earrings trying to fake it like it’s gold, and we see your ear turning green.

“And thine exactors righteousness”: an exactor is a tax collector. We’re going to be dispatched to collect the taxes from the whole planet earth and bring the wealth. We’re the exactors.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders”: because we’re going to subdue all the nations. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light”. “Thy sun shall no more go down”: our understanding ain’t going to be lost. We ain’t going to be forgetting things, ‘bro, what’s that scripture?’; none of that is going to be happening. “Neither shall thy moon withdraw itself”: the same thing.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous”: that’s some heavy stuff. You know what that means? There ain’t going to be no more menstrual cycle for the women, no more cramps. Why did the women get cramps and baby pains? Because of sin: they rebelled against Adam. In the kingdom thy people shall be all righteous. “They shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.”

“A little one shall become a thousand”: we’re going to have a whole lot of children. “And a small one a strong nation”: the same thing. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: hasten means he’s going to make it happen fast. It’s not going to take nine months to have a baby; nine months is for when you’re in your wickedness, but when you’re all righteous it’s going to be another game changer.

precepts.why: The New Testament precept. Revelation is an abbreviated version of the Old Testament, and it says the same exact thing as Isaiah 60:11: “And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there. And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it.” Isaiah says thy gates shall be open continually, not shut day nor night, that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles; Revelation says the gates shall not be shut, and they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. The wealth of the nations is brought into the kingdom of Israel.

Who are all they that despised thee? “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” We are hated of all nations. So the nations that despise us now are the ones that are going to bow themselves down at the soles of our feet: not one knee, both knees, with their face to the ground.

I the Lord will hasten it in his time: it’s not going to take nine months to have a baby. “And the children of a year old shall speak with their voices”: a year old child is going to be able to talk. “The women with child shall bring forth untimely children of three or four months old”: it ain’t going to be a nine-month thing. Three or four months old: there’s the baby boom right there. ‘Hey mom, I want some milk.’

That’s what the Bible has prophesied, and that’s why the scriptures say eye has not seen nor ear heard what the Lord has prepared. We keep thinking of the kingdom like this right here; all of what we’re going through now is going to be done away with. It’s all going to be new.

sense.text: We’re still dealing with thy kingdom come. “The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.”

“That the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains”. We look at movies like Thor and The Hobbit for the scenery and the majesty of the kingdoms they have imagined, but the Bible says the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be in the top of the mountains. There shall be no government higher than the nation of Israel. When you see Israel you’re going to have to look up; it ain’t going to be in the valley. All eyes on the planet are going to be right there: the highest mountain on the planet, higher than Mount Everest. “And shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it”: that’s still talking about Israel.

“And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law”. So why can’t the churches understand, out of Zion shall go forth the law? Why is it always some Christian garbage rhetoric about Christmas and Thanksgiving? The Bible says the law is going to go forth out of Zion.

Verse 3 is not talking about the other nations, because the other nations are referenced in verse 4. These many people that come up to learn the law are Israel.

“And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people”: here are the other nations; that’s how you know verse 3 is not talking about them. “And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks”: those are farming instruments. “Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.”

Verse 4 is talking about war. He’s going to send the 144 thousand to subdue all nations. You want peace on earth? The 12 tribes of Israel must be established in the earth and subdue the nations. There ain’t going to be no peace until that is established.

“O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.” It comes back to the house of Jacob: that’s the same thing verse 3 was saying. Come ye, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; come ye, let us walk in the light of the Lord. So we get our thoughts right: we’re still dealing with thy kingdom come.

precepts.why:
Out of Zion shall go forth the law, and Christ told you that: “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” He fulfilled the law of sacrifice; that’s what he fulfilled.

“Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.” All has not been fulfilled yet.

“Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so”: if you break the least commandments and start to teach people it’s okay to break this law, “he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them”, do and teach the law, “the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.” That’s the same thing Isaiah 2 is saying: the law goes forth in the kingdom. I want to be called great in the kingdom of heaven, men and sisters alike, so we better get our minds right.

So-called Thanksgiving comes around, near our Israelite holiday of the ingathering, tabernacles, and here comes a sister: turkeys is on sale, cranberry sauce and stuffing. Sister, get that food out of here; you want to bring your worldly mother’s abomination to the feast of God. Eat the turkey after we finish this feast, because eating it today gives the impression that we’re celebrating Thanksgiving, and Thessalonians says avoid all appearance of evil. Here comes Hanukkah, Christmas lights everywhere, ding dong and the songs, ‘it’s for the kids’. What the hell is going on here? Get your mind right.

sense.text:
Thy kingdom come: we’ve got to understand the secrets of the Lord’s prayer, what he is really talking about. “And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven”. You’ll read that and go, wait a minute, so the kingdom is coming down? But Isaiah 60 said the nations are going to build it. I’m confused.

Highlight the words “as a bride”: “prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” Remember what we read earlier: we shall no longer call him by the old name, but we shall call him my husband. Revelation 21:2 is talking about the people being as a bride adorned, not the kingdom itself. As you read further down it gets into the description of the kingdom, the same height and the same width, but that’s not what verse 2 is saying.

precepts.why: “And Sion shall come, and shall be shewed to all men, being prepared and builded, like as thou sawest the hill graven without hands.” Being what? Being prepared and builded. That is saying the same thing as Revelation 21:2: Zion, the people, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

sense.text:
“Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” The first understanding: the will of God is his law. And it begins with you and your household. Brothers want the celestial stuff God talks about; we don’t like the stuff where we have to be put in motion to do work, we just want to let the angels come. No: you want God’s will to be done on earth as it is in heaven, it starts with you men. We start with Abraham.

After we do God’s will here amongst ourselves, in our families and in our own internal thinking, then we get the promise, and part of thy will be done is that we destroy the nations.

precepts.why: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is his law. That’s the first understanding of thy will be done.

Men, listen up good. “Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him”. “For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.”

I know him, that he will command his children and his household. So the first thing, thy will be done, begins with you and your household. Abraham commanded his house to keep the way of the Lord, and that is how the Lord brought on him what he had promised.

“For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?”

We get many horror stories about sisters marrying some of you no good black ashy brothers. True story: a sister has a nice house, lovely; they get married, and the brother wants to be a carpenter: wood chips all over the house, he’s bringing trees in, holes in the ceiling, the windows of her nice car broken because he was bringing a log in. The dude is an absolute disaster and the brother can’t see it, so she says you’ve got to go, you’re destroying my life. He can’t command nobody. Brothers, you’ve got to check yourself.

On the flip side, the sister. She says she’ll put the dog outside when she marries; the brother comes home from work and there’s dog doo doo on the floor, he’s cursing her out, and she takes the dog and leaves. That’s called a dog mom: you don’t want no kids, you don’t want no husband, you want to grow old with your dog and die.

That shows we’ve got to get ourselves together; we’re not ready yet. ‘I want the Lord to come today.’ Really? You sure about that, sis, brother? Some of y’all be calling your husbands a bitch-ass, or you were just watching porn and playing with sex toys, and now you want God to come? You’ll be put to death, brother and sister. Watch what you say; you sound black jailhouse black.

The brother who wasn’t ready for marriage: about 300 pounds, can’t keep a job, gets fired every six months; that’s not marriage material. The sister said, I can fix him. We told them we couldn’t bless that, because we saw bad things happening: she was divorced with two kids and joint custody, the baby father still in the picture; you’re going to put a dress on the girl and he’s going to put pants on her, he’s going to celebrate Christmas, there’s going to be confusion. Then the baby daddy, the one she said wasn’t crazy, busted through the window late at night, took her phone and sent a blast text to all leadership describing what the two of them had been doing sexually, then threw the phone down, jumped out the window and disappeared in the night. Some of y’all will get with a woman who ain’t no damn good, with a crazy baby daddy, and put up with it. I ain’t losing my life over that.

Another story: a brother married a woman whose man was in jail; she said she’d cut him off. He comes home from work and everything is gone: the baby daddy got out of jail yesterday, and she cleared out the brother’s joint bank account, took every penny and went back to the pimp. Brothers, that’s what you have to deal with. We try to help you, but some of y’all are simps: you don’t listen, you don’t learn.

Brothers, some of y’all got no good wives; you know who they are. You choose to stay with them; fine, but don’t ever accuse us of trying to destroy your marriage. Don’t forget, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven.

“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands”: this is the no good woman, not the woman who’s trying to get herself together. “Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”: if you want to please God, remember thy will be done in earth; it says escape from her, leave her. But let’s say you say, no, I love her, I can fix it: “but the sinner shall be taken by her.” The Bible is calling you a sinner.

Make your choice, brother. If you choose the sinner route you cannot be in a leadership position. You can sit in the back, that’s fine, but you cannot be a leader among us, because you have attached sinner to yourself; you know your wife is no damn good, and everybody around you knows it.

I said all that out of love, not out of hate. The Bible calls it saving some with compassion and others by fear. That’s what we’re trying to do when we bring these situations up: save you by fear, telling you that if you don’t escape from that thing you’re going to get put to death.

“For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.” We all have need of patience, that after we have done the will of God, his law, we might receive the promise. That’s all we all want: the promise.

Why do we need patience? The verse above it: “Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward.” We all at times feel like casting away our confidence because of the things we go through: our wife leaves us, our husband leaves us, someone dies in the family, and we feel like the Lord ain’t blessing us. Don’t give up. There’s a great reward at the end of this thing, so hold on. We go through these things to teach us patience.

Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. “Fear not, thou worm Jacob”: God is calling us worms. You ever walk out early in the morning and step on a worm on the ground by accident? We are worms in this kingdom. The sisters look at us and say look at your weak bodies; we’re sickly, overweight, obese, underweight, we got diabetes, we got E.D., erectile dysfunction, everything wrong with us. “And ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.”

“Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth”: he says, don’t worry about that worm state, I’m going to change you. “Thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff”: we will destroy the nations. That’s a part of thy will be done. After we do God’s will amongst ourselves and in our families, he says, you’re going to get the promise.

Right now, with this Covid stuff, we can’t do nothing against it; to hell with Fauci, everybody knows he’s manipulating stuff, but what can we do? Right now we’re in a worm state, and we need patience to await the reward of the promise. “Thou shalt fan them”: we’re going to fan the nations, “and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them: and thou shalt rejoice in the Lord”; we’re going to be happy and glad, “and shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel.”

sense.text: “Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.” Why does it say that? Because we have not been joyful in our King. We wanted to be joyful in Joe Biden; look where that got you, Covid mandates. We wanted to be joyful in Barack Hussein Obama; that got us nowhere. Joyful in Trump; that didn’t get us nowhere either. Every king set up in this country has brought us to desolation, and we’re still looking for the next man-made king. We’ve got to be joyful in our King.
“Let them praise his name in the dance”: yes, it’s okay to dance. We’re going to praise his name in the dance.
“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people”: he don’t take pleasure in all nations on earth; he takes pleasure in his people. “He will beautify the meek with salvation.”
“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.” We ain’t going to have to wake up and do a damn nine to five. We’re going to wake up when we want to wake up.

“Let the high praises of God be in their mouth”: that’s the Bible, his laws, his testimony; that’s what’s going to be in our mouth. “And a twoedged sword in their hand”. You’ve got the Bible in your mouth and a sword in your hand: think about what’s going to happen.

“To execute vengeance upon the heathen, and punishments upon the people”: thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven. We’re going to execute vengeance upon the nations and punishments upon the peoples of this world.
“To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron”: chains, shackles. That’s thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven; this is God’s will.

“To execute upon them the judgment written”: we’re not going to do our own thoughts, ‘well, I feel like doing this today.’ We’re reading about all these various judgments in the Bible, and we have to make sure they’re executed. “This honour have all his saints”: the Bible says that’s an honour. “Praise ye the Lord”: what you got a sad face for? After you execute my judgment, you’re going to praise the Lord. Did we have to do that to them? Yes, we had to.

So they’re never going to get rid of this Bible. This Bible is going to be in the kingdom, and we’re going to read the laws out of it and put the punishments and execution upon everybody that disobeys these laws. It says the judgment written, not some other judgment: you’re going to take this same Bible and execute its justice on the planet earth. This Bible ain’t going nowhere, no matter how hard they try.

precepts.why:
We’re in the New Testament for you hypocrites. “But that which ye have already hold fast till I come”: whatever understanding we have, hold it fast, hold on to it tight, don’t let it go.

“And he that overcometh”: we’re going to overcome our personal sins, our family dilemmas, our congregational dilemmas, alcoholism, drug addiction; you men and women must overcome it. “And keepeth my works unto the end”: Christ’s works are the law; keep my works until the end. “To him will I give power over the nations”: nothing is changed from what Psalms 149 said. To him that overcomes I’m going to give power over the nations.

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”: that’s the same thing Psalms said, the same thing Isaiah 41 said about the worm Jacob made a new sharp threshing instrument. This is that thy will be done. The rod of iron is that sword we just read about in Psalms 149. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: we’re going to break the nations; we ain’t going to play with one of them. I don’t know what Bible you Christians are reading, because this is about judgment, vengeance and justice, and it’s going to go down.

“Even as I received of my Father”: Christ is the King, the Lord of lords. He’s going to be the first infantry on the front line, him and the angels. Then after the smoke clears he’s going to get the 144 and say, I’m sending y’all to China, you go to Afghanistan, you go to Palestine, you go over to Japan. We’re going to smite these nations, and we ain’t going to play with one of them, men, women or children.

This is why the nations hate us. The nations read our book. They might get on TV and say stupid stuff, but they understand. When the brothers were teaching in the Netherlands, the Arabs understood exactly what was being said, what we read in Revelation 2 and Psalms: as soon as they hear it they go, oh, they’re going to enslave us, they’re going to destroy us. So don’t think they just hate us for nothing; our brothers and sisters getting shot in the street, these are the Israelites, let’s kill them. The Haitians that just came over, why do they want to send them back? Just in case they wake up. These nations are reading the Bible.

“The portion of Jacob is not like them; for he is the former of all things: and Israel is the rod of his inheritance”: we ain’t like none of the other nations. “Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war”: that’s the same thing he said in Isaiah 41, you worm Jacob, I’m going to make you into a new sharp threshing instrument to thresh the nations. “For with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms”: Old Testament and New Testament saying the same exact thing.

“With thee also will I break in pieces man and woman”: so the women can’t say, I’m a woman, you can’t do nothing to me. Off with her head: man and woman dead. Look at them Klan films: their women support them. The white woman supports the white man in all his endeavors. In Texas, men and women together passed the law, no more abortions, for population control: our numbers got to come up, because these blacks and Latinos are beyond us. And the white man and the white woman said, let’s take slavery out of the school system so nobody knows about that; that’s a direct hit at the Israelites.

“And with thee will I break in pieces old and young; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the maid”: the young man is the teenager, and the maid the teenage girl. “And with thee will I break in pieces captains and rulers”: that’s what I want, them damn captains and rulers. We’re going to go after them. Nobody is going to escape.

“And I will execute judgments upon Moab”: Moab is the Chinese. Some of you thought the Chinese were going to get a pass; oh hell no, the Bible says I will execute judgments upon Moab. “Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance”: Edom is the so-called white man. “I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it”.

“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel”: pause right there. Christ makes the first attack, him and the angels; after that there are still going to be a lot left alive, and he’ll say, I left some alive for y’all, go forth and conquer. He’s going to dispatch the men, and the leaders of these camps are going to be Peter, James. He may break them down to smaller groups; we don’t need that many. Go forth and destroy these nations.

“And they shall do in Edom according to mine anger”: that goes back to the judgment written. Thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven: whatever the Lord says, we are going to do it. “And they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord God.” The church says the vengeance is the Lord’s, from Romans. He’s going to have the first attack, and after that he’s going to send the Israelites. Put that in your pipe and smoke it.

“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: we’re the prisoners of hope, here in America and in various other lands, always hoping for a better day, hoping for health, for safety, for longevity. The Bible says no: turn to the strong hold, and the strong hold is the Bible. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”.

“When I have bent Judah for me”: Judah ain’t going to do whatever the hell they want; he’s going to bend that tribe to his will. “Filled the bow with Ephraim”: that’s the northern kingdom; Ephraim ain’t going to do what the hell they want either, he’s going to bend them too. “And raised up thy sons, O Zion”: the other tribes of Israel, “against thy sons, O Greece”: that’s against Edom. “And made thee as the sword of a mighty man”: he’s going to make us into a new sharp threshing instrument.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them”: that’s the chariots with the angels. We don’t see that right now, so in case there are any crazy brothers in here, don’t nobody go out and do nothing stupid today. “And his arrow shall go forth as the lightning”: there’s missiles and all of that. “And shall go with whirlwinds of the south”: what they call the UFOs.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them”: God is going to defend us. “And they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones”: we’re going to devour the nations with slings and stones. “And they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine”: we’re going to make a noise like we’re drunk, laughing as we kick their butts up and down the mountains. “And they shall be filled like bowls, and as the corners of the altar.”

sense.text: “Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain”: the trumpet is the Bible. “For the day of the Lord cometh, for it is nigh at hand”: that’s what everybody’s waiting for, the day of the Lord. It’s near.

“A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, even to the years of many generations”: that’s talking about Israel.

“A fire devoureth before them”: there’s going to be fire devouring before us, “and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them”. That’s going over there into Jerusalem, the whole land of Israel; we’re going to take it back. The land of Israel is the garden of Eden. “And behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them”: nothing’s going to escape from us.
“As a strong people set in battle array”: we’re going to be decked out. We ain’t running with everybody in ragged t-shirts with holes in them; we’re going to have battle array on.
“All faces shall gather blackness”: because when we get together, we are all black.

“They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks”. Captains are having trouble trying to get brothers in ranks and in formation now; on that day, Captain Shem, you have nothing to worry about. Every man is going to be in order, decked out in battle array. It’s going to be a bad and beautiful day.

precepts.why: Proof that the land of Israel is the garden of Eden: “And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. If you’ve seen the video footage of Jerusalem, it’s a desert over there; it’s desolate, things don’t grow there, they have to import grass and trees. But it will become like the garden of Eden, “and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited.”

sense.text:
Getting the nations in order, getting these nations subdued. “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”: after Christ and the 144 get through with them, there are still going to be some nations left. They “shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

So what’s wrong with the Christians, saying you ain’t got to keep God’s high holy days, you can keep Christmas and Thanksgiving, but don’t keep God’s high holy days? What Bible are they reading? It’s telling you everybody is going to be forced to celebrate the feast of tabernacles.
“Whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.” No rain means there’s a drought, a famine, death.

“And if the family of Egypt go not up”: he gives an example with the Egyptians. If the real Egyptians decide, to hell with that, I accept him as my king but I’m not celebrating no feast of tabernacles: “there shall be the plague, wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.” “This shall be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

“And in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts.” When there shall be no more the Canaanite in Judah and in the kingdom of heaven, it means we ain’t going to be abominable; we ain’t going to be rebelling against the Lord.

precepts.why: What does it mean, there shall be no more the Canaanite? Am I African? Nope. “Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations”: we were in the midst of abominations. “Thus saith the Lord God unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan”: he said, you abominable Israelites, you’re like the Canaanites. “Thy father was an Amorite”: your father was an ashy Amorite, “and thy mother an Hittite”: your mother a bloodsucking Hittite. These are Canaanites. So no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord means Israel no longer abominable.

sense.text: “Give us this day our daily bread.” Don’t forget what came before it: ‘thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven’. Now we’re here: give us this day our daily bread, the food and raiment the Lord gives, and we are to be content with it.

precepts.why:
Our daily bread. “But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.” Some of y’all have a problem with the word content, because you say, I work at Walmart, I’m a grocery bagger, I’m not content with that. That’s not what this is talking about.

“But they that will be rich fall into temptation”: that’s the part that clears it up. One temptation is, I will steal, I will kill, I will take. Not being content will lead you into other sins of covetousness, murder, stealing. The content brother or sister will abide their time: right now I bag groceries, but in time I’m going to school; my friend over here has connections, I’m networking, I’m going to meet people and go places and be able to do things. That’s content. But when you say no, I’m gonna murder this guy over here and take his shoes, his car, you’re not content.

I’m gonna sell drugs: you can make a lot of money; some of these brothers here were drug dealers. That’s quick money, easy money, but you’re always looking over your shoulder: who’s following me, is that popo over there, is that the cops? I can’t live my life like that. That ain’t no good money.

“And a snare”: that thing on the internet, OnlyFans. Some homo brothers do it, but a lot of women do it. Our people talk about, I got a good job. What’s your job? OnlyFans. You get butt naked and you got to insert this into your oral cavity, and they pay you money to do stuff like that, and they go, I make good money. No, that’s not good money.

“And into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition. For the love of money is the root of all evil”. You want that money so bad you ain’t content, you’re gonna make it do what it do. Now you’re doing porn, you’re doing all kind of stuff. You was not content selling drugs; now you’re doing a bid, they got photos and all kind of stuff on you, and we can’t help you.

“Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches”. Some of y’all have gathered riches: you’ve worked all your life, you might have a good pension, you might have hit the lotto, grandparents left you stuff. You are what’s called rich, might be hood rich. Never, brothers and sisters, trust in uncertain riches: what you have today you might not have tomorrow. You saw what they did in Nigeria: if you don’t take the vaccine, you have no access to your banking. You might be good right now, and in your little mind that can never happen in America.

“But in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy; That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute”. Some rich people are stingy, spelled with a d, n-i-g-g-a-r-d-s, meaning stingy: this is mine, mine, mine. The Bible says be ready to distribute, “willing to communicate”: that also means distribute.

“Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come”: if you do that, you help the saints, you help this truth, and you lay in store a good foundation. Days are coming where you would have wished you helped the saints of God. “That they may lay hold on eternal life.”

“O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called”: avoid science, that’s what he’s saying. “Which some professing have erred concerning the faith”: they love white man technology with all his side effects.

sense.text:
“I have been young, and now am old”: David said, I’ve been young, but I’m an old man now, “yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.” So there should never be an Israelite man or woman in here having to beg bread. Never, ever, ever. I never want that to come to my ears, that there’s a man or a woman struggling to eat. Our job is to help.

We have pantries in the back in every IUIC school. The food is free, the Pampers is free. What’s wrong with you, talking about I need some food? There’s food back there.

precepts.why:
What David said is recorded in the book of Acts. Why did David say he never saw the righteous forsaken nor his seed begging bread? This is why: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

There’s something in that we never touch on: distribution was made unto every man according as he had need. That goes into marriage too. Some of these women say, I don’t need no man. Okay then, you stay right there by yourself. The women that were helped were the widows. They dealt with the men who had families: how big is your family? He has a family of 13, I have a family of five: his need is greater than mine. You have a family of three: my family’s needs are greater than his. Some of y’all just got a wife; you don’t have as great a need as a man who has a wife and one child.

That need doesn’t mean a man that don’t want to go out and work and wants to live off the church. That’s not what it’s talking about. It’s about a man that’s working but struggling: that man is diligent, he’s in the work, we know his name, we know him, we got to help that brother and his family. Not the brother sitting in the back, I ain’t doing nothing, or the sister with four kids saying I don’t need no man, that’s what Creflo done told me. Well, do bad by yourself.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, my servants shall eat”: my servants shall eat, “but ye shall be hungry”: but you rebellious Israelites shall be hungry. That’s what the Bible prophesies. “Behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed”. The Lord’s servants are going to eat; don’t get it twisted.

sense.text:
“And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.” A lot of times we get confused over the word debts: it’s talking about sins. All of you adulterers, adulteresses, fornicators, drug users, alcoholics, listen good: you owe the Lord a debt. We were all supposed to live godly, and we have been disobedient, every last one of us, wicked as hell, and he forgave all of us the debts we owe, because Christ paid the price.

Write this down: forgiveness doesn’t excuse or forget behavior. What forgiveness does is prevent their behavior from destroying you. If a man holds bitterness and hatred in his spirit, that could destroy him: the second I see him I bust him upside his head, I stomp his face into the ground for what they did to me and my family. You who are offended, forgive it, because if you don’t, bitterness will rise in you and destroy you.

I know it’s hard. Lord, you got to work with me, I’m gonna have to bust hot brass in that ass over there. You can be that mad, but it takes the Holy Spirit, discipline, to change that heart. Forgiveness doesn’t absolve you from judgment; forgiveness is about giving us peace of mind, so we can be at peace with ourselves. If I think about the stuff you did to me all day, I don’t have peace of mind; if I keep thinking about it, it’s going to destroy me.

precepts.why:
Let me give it to you. “Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Whoa, that’s hard for black people, Latino people to do.

“Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants.” One owed him “ten thousand talents”, of silver, but this servant didn’t have nothing to pay, so “his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had”: sell his wife, sell his snotty-nosed kids, even the house he got, and payment to be made. The servant fell down and worshipped him, begging, please have mercy on me, I’ll pay you all back. “Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.” That last word, debt: Christ is talking about sins. He forgave all of us the debts we owe.

“But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellowservants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest.” Now this is some of you. The same thing happens in reverse: have mercy on me, I’ll pay you all. “And he would not”: this is some of us in here, some of us listening. No, I’m not forgiving you. He threw him in jail till he should pay the debt.

Back in 2018 there were a lot of problems in Austin, Texas, and on false charges they had a man thrown in jail. ‘I’m sorry, brother, I’ll make it right’, and they said no, we want you in jail. This is what we’re reading about. Some of them just set up a church and try to ignore all the evil they did. Now they say, brother, I apologize, sister, I apologize, and that’s not good enough. They cast the brother into prison under false pretenses.

“O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?” The Lord is saying, I had compassion on you; shouldn’t y’all have had compassion on him? “And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due unto him. So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.”

You see how heavy that thing is. The same grace the Lord gave to you, you’re supposed to give to that man. You had the chance to go back and fix what you messed up, but you have not fixed it; you built a church upon sin, and you’re hoping people respect you, hoping people have mercy upon you. The same things you did are coming back to you: be very mindful how you’re operating the spirit. Extra mercy was given to you; why not extra mercy to that man, him and his family? Now the things Christ died for are all on you. Your sin remains.

That goes with ‘there must be offenses, but woe be unto that man by whom the offense cometh’. There are offenses that were done and never corrected, and the Most High has that written down.

sense.text: “And lead us not into temptation”. We know the Lord don’t lead people into temptation. What does it mean? It means, please don’t let us give in to temptation.

precepts.why: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” The Lord says, when you come to serve me, you better prepare yourself for temptation. We all think that when we come into this truth it’s going to be a bed of roses. Oh no: you will be tempted, you will be tried.

Remember Christ. “Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me. Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.” That was a form of temptation.

Pay attention to this: “And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.” You know what for a season means? I’ll be back, I’m not done with you. Some of us overcome a temptation and think we won. No, you didn’t win, not yet: Satan got another plan for you. I couldn’t get you through your brother, let me try your wife. And if the wife don’t work, let me try your child; that little baby is so cute, I’ll get you that way. That’s how it goes down. Lead us not into temptation: don’t let us give in to temptation.

“Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God. Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved. They on the rock are they, which, when they hear, receive the word with joy”: that’s some of you in here. “And these have no root”: you don’t study, you don’t apply. “Which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.”

That’s you brothers and sisters who are too busy in your personal lives to study. Put on the audio: YouTube got Bible chapters, we got classes seven days a week. There’s no excuse. Whether you drive a truck or you’re a cab driver, put one earplug in and leave the other one open so you can hear your customer. Because if you don’t study, you will be tempted, and in time of temptation you fall away.

“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man”: all the temptations we go through are common; there’s nothing unusual. If you’re an alcoholic, that’s a chemical temptation, drugs also. Sex, whether you’re an adulterer or a homo: sexual temptation. Stealing: you’re a thief.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”: the Lord won’t allow Satan to tempt you above that; he knows your limits. But you brothers that say, I want to teach sister such and such a scripture at her house, and we tell you bring her to the school, don’t do that, brother, and you say no, I’m disciplined, I’m strong. You go to her house, she answers the door in a see-through nightgown, and all of a sudden the Bible ends up under the bed and you and her on top of the bed. You have no root in yourselves, you don’t study, and in time of temptation you fall away. The Bible’s left under the bed.

“But will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” You have the scriptures, you got brothers you can call, sisters you can call. You ever been in the midst of sin, about to look at something on your phone, and the phone rings and there’s a brother on the line: oh, shalom. The Most High said, I’m gonna help you out here, because I see you about to give in.

“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life”: we all want the crown of life, “which the Lord hath promised to them that love him. Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God”. So when it says lead us not into temptation, that’s not the Lord doing it. James explains it: “for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.”

Lust will blind you. A brother came up a couple of months ago, talking about he’s struggling. Let me see your cell phone; go to your photos. He snatched it back: it’s a new phone, ain’t nothing really. So I know what you’re battling with; that brother’s gonna fall. Another brother got catfished by a he-she. He showed us a picture: a beautiful Dominican girl in Santo Domingo, this is gonna be my wife. She sent him pictures of herself in her bra and panties; if she repented, why is she sending you pictures like that? She was coming this week, but her uncle took her passport. How convenient. Give her a call for me: ring, ring, and either this is a dude or it’s an old lady with a frog in her throat.

When I assisted the sex crime division and robbery, we had multiple fake accounts, because the normal means you wasn’t falling for. For a man who had robbed three people, I put up Rihanna as my profile picture: meet me at the corner. Little did he know Rihanna had a bearded mustache. Stop being deceived by these internet connections, you dummies out there, men and women. He thought it was Rihanna. Simple as hell. Lust will blind you.

After the catfish class a brother came up crying: Bishop, you ruined my life, she’s going to put all my pictures on Facebook. Let me see your cell phone. All you see, to use the nice words, is his booty hole. Who the hell takes pictures like that? We had to curse the brother out. Now your booty hole’s gonna be all on the internet; you deserve to cry. There’s only so much help you can give somebody that’s stuck on stupid. Now we laughing, but there’s one or two or three sitting right here giggling that have either done it or thought about doing it. They’re doing it now, and some of you are going to do it even after hearing this, because that lust will blind you and you’re going to think, not me.

You truck-driving brothers are on the road a week at a time, away from the wife, and at these truck stops some of them be men dressed as women. He-she, whatever the hell it is, knocks on the door, and the brother says, I didn’t know what was going on, I was just horny. These are all true stories; we could write a book. Every man is tempted when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.”

sense.text: “But deliver us from evil”: that’s the part we always focus on, deliver us from evil. The judgment of life or death is the Most High’s, and against the evil coming on our people we have no power of our own. Our power is prayer, brothers and sisters; in fact that’s our only power.

precepts.why:
Deliver us from evil; let me show y’all something. “For the Lord shall judge his people”: the Lord’s going to judge us, brothers and sisters, “and repent himself for his servants”: his servants are the elect. Moses said the same thing Christ said in Matthew 24. “When he seeth that their power is gone”: when he sees that we have no power in the earth, “and there is none shut up, or left”: none doing well, being strong, being prophets.

“And he shall say, Where are their gods”: where are the gods of the Israelites now? You’re going to worship the white man, you want to follow Allah: where are their gods? “Their rock in whom they trusted, Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, and drank the wine of their drink offerings? let them rise up and help you, and be your protection.” Let those fake gods rise up and help you.

“See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.” So the judgment of life or death is the Most High’s, always. Remember that.

Listen good: “And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” The elect is the repenting Israelite. He says, for the elect’s sake I’m going to shorten the days of your persecution. That is the Lord repenting himself for his servants in Deuteronomy 32.

“And these are the words that the Lord spake concerning Israel and concerning Judah”: the two kingdoms. “We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace”: believe it or not, in this time now there’s no voice of peace. Everywhere we go there’s a voice of trembling, of fear. I’m talking about COVID, and the thing they got after it, Delta. Your friend Bill Gates had a whole list of dates: on this date there’s going to be this disease. Why? Because they’ve already been manufactured in labs.

“Ask ye now, and see whether a man doth travail with child? wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins”: because men are getting sick, “as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness”. “Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble”: this is what we’re in, the time of Jacob’s trouble. “But he shall be saved out of it”: the promise is that we shall be saved.

Think about Jacob’s trouble. When COVID came out we were all laughing, because it was only hitting white folks. A ball player got on the mic with the reporters and said, man, COVID affecting black people; next day, shazam, he had it.
