All of a sudden blacks and Latinos started getting hit left and right, and now the kids are getting hit. Nobody sees something wrong with this?

“And when he had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth beast say, Come and see. And I looked, and behold a pale horse”: this is another representation of Esau, “and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him.” Esau’s name is death. “And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth”: that’s this side of the world, Canada, North America, Central, South.

“To kill with sword, and with hunger”: with war and with famine. Venezuela, four or five years ago: Citibank went through there and opened up banks, told everybody it’s a new banking system, everybody put their money in, then the banks filed a form of bankruptcy and they lost all their money. Now a lot of the Venezuelans are going to Trinidad and other places just trying to find food to eat and work.

“And with death, and with the beasts of the earth”: death is disease, and the beasts of the earth, write this down, is zoonosis. They mix human and animal fetal tissue together to make these diseases. And guess what: we have no power to do anything against it. Our power is prayer.

Deliver us from evil. “Therefore I endure all things for the elect’s sakes”: Paul said, I endure all things for them. Listen good, especially you brothers. “That they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory. It is a faithful saying: For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us”.

“But thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience”: examine that. “Persecutions, afflictions”: you’ve known the persecutions I’ve been through; that’s the apostle Paul. “Which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me.” We just read in Corinthians that he’ll make a way to escape: when Paul was catching hell, the Most High was delivering him.

“Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” I want all you men and women to meditate on that verse, you lily lollipop brothers and sisters. You want the kingdom of heaven, you shall suffer persecution. There’s no getting around it: if you want this kingdom that’s coming, you must suffer persecution. That goes for you women too; you are not absolved from this. A lot of you ain’t been through nothing yet, but you shall be persecuted. That’s what the prophecy says.

sense.text: “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” When it says no torment touch them, that’s talking about the lake of fire, that eternal condemnation.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”. This year alone over 20 brothers and sisters died in IUIC, and the unwise see that they die and say, God judged them, because he’s wicked, she’s wicked; that’s why God did that to them. “And their departure is taken for misery”: your departure, your death, is taken as misery.
“And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” The righteous are in peace.
“For though they be punished in the sight of men”: it looked like they were punished in the sight of man, “yet is their hope full of immortality.”

“And having been a little chastised”. You mean John the Baptist being beheaded was a little chastised? Yes. You mean Peter and his wife being crucified upside down was a little chastised? Yes. Why was it little? Because of what verse one said: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and torment shall not touch them. Being beheaded, crucified, COVID-19, diabetes, affliction, whatever it is, touches the body, not the soul. “They shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.”

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” This brings it to the next level of understanding. Received as a burnt offering: that’s death. The death of the saint is an offering to the Most High God.

We see death different than what the Bible teaches. That Sam Cooke song, ‘I don’t know what’s up there beyond the sky’: everybody’s scared. Our forefathers said no: the time of my departure is at hand, it’s time for me to go. They didn’t fear, oh, I’m going to be killed. Read of the seven sons: they kept saying, cut my hands off, and it’s like, what’s wrong with these dudes? But at the end they said, ‘we shall have a resurrection, but you shall have no resurrection to life’. Our forefathers knew something we have forgotten.

In this time of persecution, this time of Jacob’s trouble, the Most High is going to take us to that understanding. He said, you’ve been looking at death wrong; there’s a lot of things you don’t see too clear, but I’m going to show you now, because you’re crying out to me.

precepts.why: “For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.” This is heavy. Paul used the same words: I’m ready to be offered, and the time of my departure, the time of my death, is at hand. So that death is an offering: received as a burnt offering, the death of the saint is an offering to the Most High God.

Look at the torment, so you understand the difference between you being beheaded, crucified, COVID-19, diabetes, affliction, and the torment. “If any man worship the beast”: any man worship the white man, “and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead”: you receive his mark, his policies, in your mind, “or in his hand”: you support it. “The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God”: you’re going to get judged. Let’s see what kind of judgment.

“Which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone”: tormented, the same word we just read in Wisdom of Solomon 3. “In the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb”: in the presence of Christ. “And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever”: your torment shall be forever and ever. “And they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.” That is the torment that shall not touch the souls of the righteous.

Don’t fear them that kill the body, because that’s the fear we all fear; but the Lord says no, that ain’t the fear. “And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”: Revelation 14 was talking about your soul. When I mentioned John the Baptist and Peter, I was talking about their body, not their soul. “But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” Hell is the lake of fire; that’s what you don’t want.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” It uses the same words as Wisdom of Solomon 3:6. When we break it down, we always leave it at you’re being tempted by lust or money, sex, drugs, alcohol, and we leave it there. It’s deeper than that: Wisdom of Solomon brings it to the next level of understanding.

“Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.” That’s the precious thing. The Lord said, here’s another offering. John got beheaded: that’s an offering to me. Peter and his wife got crucified upside down: I love that smell. Christ was the greatest; his offering took it all.
“And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.” The apostle James was killed with the sword, and the Lord said, an offering, another offering.

sense.text: Still dealing with deliverance from evil. “Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you”. Who’s troubling us? The United States government, with Fauci. Not just him: the CDC, the NIH, and Fauci’s filthy wife is over one of those damn things. They’re creating all these: oh, we got a new vaccine; you had one yet? We got two more for you. The hell is this?
“And to you who are troubled rest with us”: come into this truth, learn. “When the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels”.
“In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ”: that’s the Israelites right there.
“Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power”: we just read that in Revelation 14.

“For thine is the kingdom”. The kingdom shall be the Lord’s when Esau goes down. When they go down, the kingdom of God will be ushered in, set up and established on this earth. They got to go down. That’s Esau’s end of the world, but Jacob is the beginning of the world that cometh thereafter.

precepts.why: “Thine, O Lord, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O Lord”. Thine is the kingdom, O Lord.
“And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau”: and Esau’s judged. “And the kingdom shall be the Lord’s”: the kingdom shall be the Lord’s when Esau goes down.

Obadiah 21 and Revelation 12 are saying the same thing, but Revelation is not using the word Esau; it uses another word. “And the great dragon was cast out”: remember the dragon with seven heads and ten horns, “that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world”: everybody’s got to get a mandatory vaccine. “He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: his angels are his allies, France, Europe, Germany, all of them.

“And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation”: once Esau is cast down, now has come salvation, “and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ”. The kingdom of our God is what we want to stress: when they go down, the kingdom of God will be ushered in and set up and established on this earth.

sense.text: “For thine is the kingdom, and the power”: thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power.

precepts.why: “Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power”: we’re the people. We might pray once a day, we think about the Lord, we hardly study. But as you sit around and see the death going through the country, going through the world with our people, like in IUIC alone, 20 people died this year. We ain’t there yet, because we don’t have the fear. When more of us start dying, we’re gonna turn to the Lord: you’re gonna stop with the porn, you’re gonna stop with the alcohol and drug addiction. It ain’t hit home yet, but when it hit home. A lot of us ain’t willing, because a lot of you think you can’t be touched by the finger of God.

That don’t mean you’re condemned. Let me show you something about death: “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” All things includes death. When death comes through, see the good that comes behind it: you know that brother or sister is with the Lord in paradise. And the good that’s for you is, let me get myself right, because if it happened to him, if it happened to her, surely it could come this way.

What Joseph said: what you meant for evil, what the white man meant for evil. “But as for you, ye thought evil against me”, when his brothers sold him into slavery, “but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.” When the Lord allowed the patriarchs to sell Joseph into slavery it seemed so evil, which it was, but there was a divine purpose behind it nobody could see. Joseph said, I’m in slavery here, I’m in prison almost 20 years, but the purpose is for me to be risen up and to save the Israelites from death. He saw the spiritual meaning behind it.

We got to start to look at things that seem to go wrong in our lives and say, the Lord’s trying to teach me something, or teach brothers and sisters around me something. That’s how we got to start to look.

sense.text: “For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.” The glory: our God is our glory.

precepts.why: We read this earlier. “The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.” Our God, our glory.
Saying the same thing: “And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.”
